lines.x: Your assistant? You mean you want a sick little kid who can't even read all her letters to share your workload? Or are you afraid I'll cause trouble again, so you want me where you can watch me? No, no, I've got no objections. It's your call. You're the boss, after all.

Why are you so much taller than me? If I stood and stared at you while you were dozing, would you have nightmares? Would you even notice? Tch, what a shame. Can you give me some thumbtacks to play with? I promise you won't feel a thing— Ahem, I promise I won't stick you with them!

The power tier of Deity Grypherburg is stuffy and hot. I used to clean the Originium pipes down there for people, and I picked up plenty of beetles and butterflies that had been trapped and died in them—don't worry, I'm not carrying them on me. Hah, I was so stupid back then. I actually thought I was luckier than the bugs. But the fact that I was down there at all means we were exactly the same.

I don't feel like talking right now. It's nothing to do with my mood, it's just—let's say I'm talked out, alright? I'm thinking about something. Something that has nothing to do with you. I don't want snacks, stop talking to me! Ugh, now I've lost my train of thought! Let me see what snacks you've got, then. Never mind. Want to go buy some from the vending machine together?

Boring, boring, boring. Why do all these 'documents' look exactly the same? Is this what you look at every single day... How sad. Want to play marbles for a bit? No, no, these are mine, I can't lend them to you. You'll have to go outside and find your own.

This fowlbeast doesn't have a name. What do you mean, why? It isn't my pet, and it isn't merchandise in a shop, so why would it need a name? It stays by me, and not for food or warmth either. Maybe tomorrow it won't come at all. Nothing's ever certain.

Did you ever find whoever swiped the blades off the stationery shelf? What a shame. Still, you're right—people are drawn to shiny things. I read it in Matvey's study notes: some nobles will even hire someone to rob and kill over a single necklace. No, I never said it was me.

Cookies and hot tea—are you trying to buy me off? Smooth things over, with who? You've got it wrong, I don't dislike Rosalind. She just nearly beat Antosha into a puddle of Originium Slug jelly, that's all. No, I'm not exaggerating. And if you really do want to buy me off, try blades, pins, or moth specimens instead.

The book Matvey gave me? No, there's no grand philosophy in it, just some of the things he and Antosha went through. I read it very slowly—or rather, I'm not all that willing to read it. I know what you want to ask. Yes, I miss them. I always will. But I'd still rather hear him tell it himself.
Oh my, I didn't mean to scare you. I've been standing here watching you for quite a while—ever since you first fell asleep. What's wrong?

So you're boss Sonya's boss? Just call me Ukusik. Sonya says you're impressive, though you don't look like you could take her in a fight. Fine, don't worry—if it ever came to blows, I'd help you. What are you laughing at?
Which street corner did you get this off? The picture's so crisp, and there's no weird watermark either... What do you mean, it isn't a bootleg? And it isn't a movie either?!

This is for me? The style's so old-fashioned—are you sure you didn't grab the wrong one? Oh, it's a promotion medal. Fine, thank you. A speech? Uh, then let's go with 'I'll keep working hard.' Try to get me a prettier one next time.

Another medal for me? Not bad. If it rained again, today would be perfect. Check the forecast? Sigh—the newspaper in my hand is just a prop for blending in. Do you really want to know what the weather was like in Deity Grypherburg eight years ago?
Hsss—nobody warned me there'd be this many people.
No need to stare at me. Just get on with your own work.

Someone always has to be hard-hearted enough to hurt other people's feelings, and someone always has to heal those wounded hearts—so everyone gives something up, don't they? Don't worry, I'll treat them properly.
Shh—keep it down. Enemy movement? I wouldn't know. I just wanted a little quiet.
Let's go with that. Stop hesitating.
You're the boss. Your call.
By your—command.
Of—course.
I know you're not afraid of pain, but try this anyway—much better, isn't it?
Hey! Don't you hit my patient! What? That guy isn't on our side?
Yes, hit them just like that! Don't be scared, I'm right here!
I'll stitch up the wound. Relax, I'll make it a pretty one.
This time you really do deserve to pat yourself on the back, boss.
Look how nervous you were. I told you I'd help you!
What are you looking at me for? Do you want to hear my assessment, or shall we skip it? Tch—what if I'd been planning to praise you?
I smell danger—did somebody put on perfume? If not, then the enemy must be catching up. Let's run.
It's too bright. I need a corner the light doesn't reach... That's just what I like. Got a problem?
Have you washed your hands? I'm not saying you're dirty—I just finished sorting my collection. To be safe, you'd better wash them again in a bit.
No comment. Yes, you haven't asked yet, but that doesn't change my answer... Oh, fine, ask away, ask away. Look at that face— No, really, what were you going to tell me? Come on, tell me!
Arknights.

I don't like New Year's meat jelly or pies, but I'm rather fond of the custom where you write a wish on a slip of paper and burn it. I always used to write 'somewhere to live,' and then I met Antosha. Later I changed it to 'enough to eat,' and I ended up here. And now? I'm not telling you!
Strange, I keep feeling like I'm being watched... You're just in time. Take a look at the humidifier on your desk—doesn't it seem a bit off? It doesn't? No way, no way. My instincts are always right!

Ah, you caught me. I was going to sneak it in here before you got to the office. Here—a rag doll I sewed to look like you. Cute, isn't it? You do look after me, after all. Happy birthday! What do you mean, you're not used to me talking like this? Hey! You explain yourself!

'The road.' Antosha taught me that word many times over, trying to make its meaning clear to me, but Matvey would always stop him, saying you can't understand it just from hearing someone talk about it—better to go and see for yourself, to walk it yourself. Doctor, I've seen a great deal aboard Rhodes Island. And I want to walk further still.
